definitions.explanation: The state of something not yet being completed. Used for works of art, buildings, projects, and other things that are still in progress or were left unfinished.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}は{未完成|みかんせい}だ。
{未完成|みかんせい}のまま{放置|ほうち}されている{建物|たてもの}がある。
examples.english: There is a building that has been left unfinished.

examples.japanese: シューベルトの「{未完成|みかんせい}」は{二|に}つの{楽章|がくしょう}しかないが、{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{愛|あい}されている{名曲|めいきょく}だ。
examples.english: Schubert's 'Unfinished' has only two movements, but it is a masterpiece beloved around the world.

notes:
USAGE:
{未完成|みかんせい} can function as a noun ({未完成|みかんせい}のまま "while still unfinished") or as a na-adjective ({未完成|みかんせい}な{作品|さくひん} "an unfinished work"). The noun usage is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未完成|みかんせい}のまま: left unfinished
- {未完成|みかんせい}の{作品|さくひん}: unfinished work
- {未完成|みかんせい}の{建物|たてもの}: unfinished building
- まだ{未完成|みかんせい}だ: it's still incomplete

CONTRAST:
{未完成|みかんせい} (incomplete) is the opposite of {完成|かんせい} (completion, finished). The prefix {未|み} indicates "not yet" and appears in many similar words: {未定|みてい} (undecided), {未来|みらい} (future/not yet come), {未熟|みじゅく} (immature).
